title: Intuitionistic first-order natural deduction

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Syntax and semantics of predicate logic; Natural Deduction (handout 8)

summary: Construct first-order natural-deduction certificates with genuine constructive connectives, protected quantifier parameters, equality and admissible proof operations.
abstract: A proof that an object exists may name a witness, while a proof about every object must leave its chosen object arbitrary. Intuitionistic first-order deduction keeps both forms of reasoning without treating the impossibility of nonexistence as an existence proof. We define finite proofs with explicit witness terms and fresh parameters, include the ordinary substitution rules for equality, and show how entire proofs change under renaming and substitution. A reserve of temporary names handles languages without constants. The resulting calculus extends constructive propositional deduction, supports proofs from arbitrary sets through finite subsets, and keeps the extra rule of classical contradiction separate.
